the effects of catecholamines and aging on beta-adrenergically mediated cAMP responses in human mononuclear leukocyte.
the role of the sympathetic nervous system in the regulation of the cardiovascular system.
the effects of aging and disease on the regulation of beta-adrenoceptor signaling.

the beta-adrenergically mediated responses of mononuclear leukocyte are altered by age.
the beta-adrenergics receptors in the elderly are not different than the young.
beta-adrenergics and cAMP are involved in acute regulation of cardiovascular function, but that this is altered with age, perhaps due to catecholamine-induced alterations in signal transduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acute regulation of beta adrenergic responses is affected by age.
acute regulation of beta- adrenergic receptor function in human mononuclear leukocyte is affected by age.
acute beta-adrenergically mediated regulation of the cardiovascular system is impaired in the elderly.

beta-adrenergics are important in the elderly and that their function can be modulated.
the acute regulation of adrenoceptor signaling in leukocytes is affected by age and that this may be relevant to the study of acute regulation of cardiovascular function in older adults.
